title: Sunny and the Stone Curlew | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka finds a bush stone-curlew standing perfectly still in the moonlight, its great golden eyes watching everything and nothing, and the two of them share the quietest moment in the whole bush. A calming bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The stone curlew had been standing there for a very long time.

Sunny could tell by how still it was. Perfect stillness takes practice.

It stood in a patch of pale moonlight at the edge of the clearing — a tall, thin bird with long yellow legs and enormous golden eyes. It did not move when Sunny approached. It barely seemed to breathe.

Sunny stopped a few paces away.

The curlew's great eyes looked at her. They were the colour of old gold — deep and round and utterly calm.

Neither of them moved.

The bush was quiet around them. A moth passed between them, and they both watched it go, and then looked back at each other.

Sunny felt something settle inside her. The curlew's stillness was catching. She felt herself go quiet in the same way — all the little thoughts and rustlings inside her going still.

The curlew blinked — very slowly.

It opened its beak just a little, and called — one soft, low note — not to Sunny, but to the bush at large. To the night. To no one in particular. Just a quiet acknowledgement: I am here. The night is good.

Then it was still again.

Sunny sat down very slowly. The curlew watched.

The moon moved a fraction higher.

And Sunny, wrapped in the curlew's deep stillness, closed her eyes and slept.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, stone curlew. Goodnight, little one.
